clue.text: Horse cut in two by taxi. How gruesome!

indicators.note: the horse is split into two parts with the taxi placed between them

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A cab ploughs into a horse, slicing it in half, and an onlooker recoils in horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Something macabre dwells grimly on death and horror, which is what gruesome describes.

clue.text: Ill feeling when made to solve 1000+1+51

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: the pieces made from the sum are rearranged, as if solving a puzzle, into a new word

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
LI is the Roman numeral for fifty-one

explanation.surface: Someone forced to do an awkward sum resents it.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum looks like arithmetic, but each number stands for letters: Roman numerals, and a card worth one. 'Made to solve' scrambles the last two pieces into ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spite or a wish to harm, a form of ill will.

clue.text: Cover for article in magazine issue

indicators.note: the article sits in the middle of the magazine issue, one word placed inside the other

parts.note: a single copy of a magazine is one issue of it
an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A feature in a magazine number has been chosen for the front cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering, such as one over a bed or throne.

clue.text: Spend all one's shekels and let everyone go hang

definitions.meaning: to squander every coin of one's money in a single go
to stop caring about anyone, damning the whole crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Spending all one's money at once, and also an exasperated cry consigning everyone to damnation.

clue.text: Divorcee everyone rises to praise

parts.note: a former spouse is called an ex

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the lot means everyone or everything

explanation.surface: A former wife and all her friends stand to applaud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rises' turns LOT upwards in this down entry, making TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify, a stronger synonym of praise.

clue.text: Doctor Dean admitted act and went elsewhere

annotationWithheld.why: Doctor Dean admitted act and went elsewhere (5,2): MOVED ON parses as MO (doctor) + DON inside which VE is admitted, but no clue word gives VE ('act' does not), and DEAN has an A the answer lacks; likely an OCR misread no search resolved
annotationWithheld.clue: Doctor Dean admitted act and went elsewhere

clue.text: Niggardly dandy has good intentions

parts.note: a niggardly person is stingy, that is mean
a swell is a fashionable, smartly dressed man

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted fop is nonetheless well-meaning at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean here is the British sense: stingy with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who means well has kindly aims even when the outcome disappoints.

clue.text: Serve a large portion of meat

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request to dish up a generous helping of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the flesh of a calf eaten as food.

clue.text: Suit for a girl's best friend

definitions.meaning: one of the four card suits in a pack
the song lyric praising precious jewels as what a girl loves most

explanation.surface: Seeking the right outfit for a woman's closest companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are a playing-card suit, and the song 'Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend' calls the gems exactly that.

clue.text: What a bridge player may call anything but buttocks

definitions.text: What a bridge player may call

parts.note: anything but means not, the negation
rumps are the hindquarters or buttocks

explanation.surface: A card player's bid is described as anything other than a rude word for the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a contract with no trump suit is a bid of no trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid of no trumps is a contract played without any trump suit, a call made in the auction.

clue.text: Hutton had to play slowly

parts.note: Len Hutton was a famous England cricket captain
taken as written

explanation.surface: The cricketer Hutton was forced to bat cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Len Hutton was a celebrated English cricketer, so 'play slowly' suggests stodgy batting, but it is the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is an Italian tempo marking telling musicians to perform at a slow pace.

clue.text: Make criticisms and rush away from the others

parts.note: to tear is to rush along at great speed
apart means separated from the rest

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault and storms off to stand alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear apart a piece of work is to criticise it savagely.

clue.text: Tell a better story to a lean investor

parts.note: to cap it is to top someone's tale with a better one
to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: An investor is outdone by a rival's tall tale about a thin colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' is the verb (as a ship lists), not the adjective for thin.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist puts money into business ventures to make a profit.

clue.text: Staple food in Kyoto, Fukayama and elsewhere

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the place names that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A tourist note on an everyday dish eaten in Japanese cities and beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of Kyoto into Fukayama.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, bean curd, is a basic everyday foodstuff across East Asia.

clue.text: Suit — the policeman?

definitions.meaning: to be suitable or satisfy a requirement
would suit the police, the Bill being British slang for the police

explanation.surface: Would this outfit please the constable?
explanation.walkthrough: The Bill (the Old Bill) is British slang for the police, so the phrase read cryptically means to suit them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be just right for a requirement; read playfully it means to be the right size for the police.

clue.text: Become afraid to belch

definitions.meaning: read literally, to bring wind up from the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for growing anxious, which read literally describes bringing up gas.

clue.text: Gave evidence to examine whether I had secreted note

parts.note: to test is to examine
if can mean whether

indicators.note: secreted means hidden away, so the note is tucked inside the contraction

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A witness in court tested whether a musical note had been hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give statements under oath as a witness.

clue.text: Auction of a reservoir containing water

parts.note: a dam holds back a reservoir, standing for it here
a sale is an auction

explanation.surface: A water company auctions off a reservoir and everything in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auction of a reservoir' read as A DAM SALE; Adam's ale is old slang for drinking water, Adam having had nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous old name for plain drinking water.

clue.text: How Blackbeard appeared to draw breath

parts.note: as can mean in the manner of, answering how
Blackbeard was a notorious pirate, standing for one here

explanation.surface: Blackbeard's appearance is so frightening that people gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the end; the rest reads as a description of the famous buccaneer's look.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate is to breathe in or pronounce a sound with a puff of breath.

clue.text: Very upset by record playing well into the night

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
on means playing, as a record is on
so late describes an hour far into the night

explanation.surface: A neighbour is distraught at a record blaring until the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means inconsolably sad, deeply unhappy.

clue.text: Soldiers turn up with many a traveller

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reads the soldiers' letters upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops arrive along with numerous wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reverses OR to RO in this down entry; 'turn up' wants to mean arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany people are traditionally nomadic, often called travellers in Britain.

clue.text: To commit a crime is beyond the limit

parts.note: off can mean away from or beyond
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Breaking the law is said to go too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to break a law or transgress.

clue.text: One taken in by fellow premier

indicators.note: taken in by says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a man is a fellow
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone duped by a chap who heads the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests deceived; here it puts I inside MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Main and premier are both adjectives meaning chief or principal.

clue.text: Go mad and sky the ball onto the pavilion

definitions.text: sky the ball onto the pavilion
definitions.meaning: a cricket hit landing on top of the pavilion building

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for exploding with anger, and literally a cricket shot that strikes the pavilion's top.

clue.text: Fabric for a sentimental little daughter

parts.note: twee means sweetly sentimental
D is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: Cloth chosen for a soppy young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Twee is British for cloyingly cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth.

clue.text: Many varieties of Asian starling

indicators.note: varieties means different arrangements of the letters of the word before

explanation.surface: Asia is home to many kinds of starling.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling of southern Asia known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Whenever I want it, my tea ain't made

indicators.note: the tea is made from these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demanding person insists on tea on request, complaining it has not been brewed.
explanation.definitionFit: At any time and whenever both mean on whatever occasion.

clue.text: Statue produced one minute before time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A sculpture appears moments before the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a carved likeness of a person, such as a statue.

clue.text: Mere lad developed into a real gem

indicators.note: developed means the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A mere boy has grown into a fine young man.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone.

clue.text: Held up by non-clerical entry in legal document

indicators.note: an entry made in something sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
lay means not of the clergy

explanation.surface: Proceedings stalled by a layman's addition to a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Delayed and held up both mean made late.
